h3. *Micromobility legal threats due to insurance claim rejections*

* Tier 1 escalates to Tier 2

According to ch. 23 § 2 of the Code of Procedure, the Police Authority must collect evidence during a preliminary investigation to investigate who can reasonably be suspected of a crime and whether there are sufficient grounds for prosecution.
The police authority may collect and process personal data in order to investigate and prosecute crimes according to ch. 2. 1 § 2 of the Act (2018:1693) on the police's processing of personal data within the scope of the Criminal Data Act.

Information in an ongoing preliminary investigation is subject to confidentiality in accordance with the provisions in ch. 18. 1 and 35 chap. §§ 1 of the Publicity and Confidentiality Act (2009:400). After some research and testing different scenario that involve not only Trip Recording and VoIP calls, but also other type of a concurrent use of a microphone I discovered that the issue is not related to the Driver app specifically, but it was the version of Android the Driver app was installed on. Below there is a short summary of this research and a follow up solution how we should approach to this issue.

According to the Android [documentation|https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/media/platform/sharing-audio-input] there are two major cases for the shared microphone use:

* On {{Android 9}} and before there is no shared microphone use, so who first acquired the microphone will use it. The others won't be able to start a recording session and it end up with error.  The exception is a GSM call that can interrupt any microphone session.
* On {{Android 10}} and above there is a concept of a shared microphone use, but different clients cannot read data from the microphone at the same time (in the majority of the cases). Different use cases for the microphone use may have different priorities. The use case with a higher priority will receive data from the microphone and the use case with a lower priority will receive silence. Two use cases with the same priority (at least in my tests) work by {{first come, first served}} rule. Very simplified the priorities look the following:

# Built-in voice assistant
# GSM call
# VoIP communication
# Anything else (eg. recording voice messages, trip recording, etc).

Considering the information above I tried to reproduce the same scenario swapping the client apps on my test devices (i.e. I installed Rider on Android 9 and Driver on Android 13) and the issue did reproduce exactly the same except now Rider could not be heard while Trip recording was active. This proved that the issue is not in a particular client app, but in the Android 9 platform that cannot share a microphone access.

*Bottom line:* this bug will affect any of our users on Android 5 - Android 9, no matter if it’s a Rider or a Driver. The user with a {{trip audio recording}} active won't be heard by the other VoIP call participant, while the other VoIP call participant will be heard perfectly well.

----

What we can do knowing everything above:

*Solution 1*: We consider {{VoIP calls}} less important than {{Trip audio recording}}. 

Before starting a VoIP call (incoming or outgoing) we check if there is a trip audio recording active and we block the call from being started: we inform the Comms backend that the trip recording is active, the backend doesn’t provide VoIP call contact option (with a fallback to Phone Masking) to both Rider and Driver and if an incoming call is received we just reject it automatically.

*Solution 2*: We consider {{VoIP calls}} more important than {{Trip audio recording}}. 

We inform the engineers of the Rider and Driver teams about the issue. They start observing the current VoIP call state that our VoIP component already provides. 

* When the trip audio recording is already started and there is an incoming or outgoing VoIP call is about to be started, the recording is paused. When the VoIP call is finished, the recording is resumed.
* When the VoIP call is currently in progress and user tries to start trip audio recording, a warning pop-up informs the user that recording cannot be started until the call is finished. Alternatively they may show an info pop-up telling that the recording will be started automatically when the call is finished and then they start observing the VoIP call state.

The *Solution 1* will require effort from the Comms team only, but will include also the effort from the Backend side. The *Solution 2* will require Product decisions from the Rider/Driver teams as they will need to decide how the recording flow will be interrupted and resumed. There could be changes in the user experience (if some pop-ups are needed to be displayed) so probably a UX expert’s input can be considered. It will also include the engineering effort from the Rider/Driver team, however because the bug affects our feature more than theirs we may consider taking the engineering effort to Comms and contribute to the clients' teams repositories (but the Product and the UX expect input is needed anyways)

Hi [~accountid:712020:ab95f96b-73f1-4bb8-a5fd-5178ef3f1339] and sorry for the late reply. 

As described in [this short memo|https://docs.google.com/document/d/14P5h54rPcn_e6hh3fK0w6FwZgM4OKMa7Adst5vPCGs0/edit], the TVDE law allows *only* light passenger vehicles (EU category M1) to operate . According to the Road Traffic Code, such vehicles must weight more than 550kg. 

If I understand correctly the traffic buster vehicle’s weight is 305kg and its type of vehicle has already been classified as an L6e, which is [considered by the IMT|https://www.imt-ip.pt/sites/IMTT/Portugues/Veiculos/Aprovacoes/HomologacoesVeiculos/Paginas/HomologacaoVeiculos.aspx] as a “light quadricycle”, thus *not allowed for the TVDE activity.* 

Plus, according to the [European regulation on the approval and market surveillance of motor vehicles|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32018R0858], Art. 23 says: 

* “Only one application shall be submitted in respect of a particular type of vehicle, system, component or separate technical unit. That single application shall be submitted in only one Member State and to only one approval authority therein.”
* “The approval authority shall reject an application for a type-approval of a different type designation or of a modification with respect to a previous application where the changes are not sufficient to constitute a new type of vehicle, system, component or separate technical unit”.

So as [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] said, the traffic buster is not in accordance with the TVDE Law. The inclusion of such types of vehicles in the upcoming law review should be one of our asks.

La loi sur la protection des données donne aux individus le droit d'obtenir une copie de leurs données personnelles dans le cadre de la recherche - c'est-à-dire des données personnelles qui les identifient ou qui permettent de les identifier en tant que personne physique vivante.

Par exemple, ce droit ne doit pas porter atteinte aux droits d'autrui, y compris à nos secrets commerciaux ou à notre propriété intellectuelle, et en particulier au droit d'auteur protégeant le logiciel. En outre, nous devons souligner que si, après une analyse approfondie, nous concluons que nos droits ou les droits d'autrui prévalent, nous ne serons pas en mesure de vous donner accès à certains documents lorsqu'une dérogation s'applique.

Nous partagerons des copies des données personnelles que nous détenons à votre sujet et auxquelles vous avez droit. Sont inclus :
*Documents d'identité*

*Profil du conducteur, enregistrement, informations sur les contrôles*

*Données relatives aux blocs*

*Détails de la facturation*

*Enregistrement du journal des modifications*

*Historique des appareils du conducteur*

*Historique des déplacements du conducteur*

*Taux de confirmation*

*Préférences de répartition du conducteur*

*Journal de bord du conducteur*

*Offres et inscriptions des conducteurs*

*Historique de la voiture sélectionnée*

*Temps passé par le conducteur dans le statut*

*Note moyenne*

HI

Rider discount netting against the commission charged from the drivers and fleets is a mechanism for providing discounts to the riders in a way that they could also be included as discounts to the aggregated commission (partner) invoices in order for Bolt to be able to reduce the VAT amount paid to the tax office. Since we have commission invoices only in intermediate billing model, rider discount netting can only occur in intermediate model. It is set up on invoice issuer level and can be partial (only a given percentage of the rides with discounts would be selected for netting).

Without rider discount netting the rider discount is provided by Bolt and displayed as a discount in the total section of the rider invoice from the driver to the rider.

With rider discount netting the rider discount is provided by the driver and is displayed as an invoice row on the rider invoice. Bolt compensates the discount amount to the driver or the fleet and it is added to the aggregated commission (partner) invoice as a discount from the charged commission amount. As a result the VAT amount is also smaller on the commission invoice.  

[^COMM-Netting Rider Bonuses-011223-074640.pdf]

The result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts.

After discussing with [~accountid:5aab754b5c335d2a73a795f4] and [~accountid:5f1538051c682d00295dbb61], we’ve decided go ahead with changing the Reportables logic globally for Ride-Hailing tool.

* Reportables section will be a *mandatory* field for all *High-risk* and *Significant*-*risk* cases
* We’ll have options *_Injury_*, *_Fatality_*, *_No_*
* Upon ticking *Injury,* the agent will be presented with injury severity types that match the current MM ones (excluding the types _No Injury_ and _Fatality_ as they are separate Reportables)

|First Aid Injury|An event in which someone has gotten injured, but the injury is limited to bruising/scratches that can be treated by the person themselves with first aid.|
|Medical Treatment Injury|An event in which someone has gotten injured and required to be medically looked at by a professional (ambulance is called or the person is taken to the hospital).|
|Injury Impacting Lifestyle|Injury Impacting Lifestyle - an event in which someone has gotten injured and the injuries sustained will likely or have already caused them to miss work due to being "out of comission" while they recover.|
|Permanent Disability|An event in which someone has gotten injured and the injuries sustained have or will cause them to be permanently disabled.|

* In terms of escalating cases to crisis channels, we’ll still have pre-defined Event Categories that are deemed potential crisis (we’ll review them to ensure we have global cohesion)
* Reportables will be a separate data point in the escalation triggers, to make the reported level of injury visible.
* Once this is live, we can review the escalation ECs and escalate some ECs (like Robbery and Accidents) _ONLY_ if there has been some injury.

So for more context, we have rolled out Onboarding Guidance and re-training for drivers on the platform. The onboarding guidance is a 5-day module for drivers to go through once they are logged into the app and are presented with the home screen. Drivers then are enrolled to the guidance, for the next 5 days, they receive guidance modules, which focus on different topics, them being as follows:

* Day 1 - Essentials (basic information about the platform and it’s functions)
* Day 2 - Balance (more detailed about balance and it’s features)
* Day 3 - Safety (general safety tips + features)
* Day 4 - On the road (quality) (quality metrics + features)
* Day 5 - Self-help (personal info + articles + support contact)


Re-trainings are focused on educating drivers when they hit a certain threshold, such as when their Acceptance Rate drops to a certain level, Driver Score or they have been reported by a rider to CS regarding Unsafe Driving, we offer Stories in the app, which serve as a sort of warning to them, that they should start working on improving their statistics using the following suggestions on the re-trainings. 



There have been some mentions from Local Operations asking if we have any CS articles that could be shared with IH and OS agents, so that they can ensure they take the correct steps in helping drivers troubleshoot it and escalate only if needed.

*Reasons why are we doing this -*


# We have millions of legacy invoices spread across billing verticals (verticals, for which invoices have been migrated to Billing Document). And the only way to access these invoices is via PHP Admin (view and pdf download). We have a push to get rid of PHP Admin, therefore having these PDFs in S3 and accessible from somewhere else is one reason why we are doing this
# Another reason is that having this would mean our life is simpler and easier when we have to provide invoices in bulk. (Food for thought: Should this be used only for legacy invoices or for Billing Document Invoices too; cost vs benefit analysis)
# One more benefit is that this avoids issue with backward compatibility given our invoices are by definition immutable (from both data and representation perspective).



*What does this mean?*

We need to investigate the scope of storing invoices in S3 as immutable objects and what benefit it provides, what problems it solves, and what problems it generates.


*Questions -*

# It seems as per this solution we are not moving the underlying data in various invoice tables in billing verticals. Is there an alternative approach like migrate this data to Billing Document? It would be good to evaluate this - also while doing that think of questions such as -
## What sequence of public id will be used for such exported data?
## What will happen to access via links already sent?
# What will happen to current access via links already sent? Will be rely on users reaching to CS for accessing their legacy invoices? Or will we route the same endpoint to S3
# Fiscalization - 
## Will the PDF stored in S3 will be Fiscalized one or Bolt one for Fiscal markets?
## Since we already store fiscalized PDF in S3 on Fiscalization side do we need to store again on core side?
## In order to answer b) it is important to think how tooling on top of this will work. For example if you have bulk download which downloads from S3 using metadata that is applicable to this bucket it may be wise to store them here too to keep things simple.
# What about fallback logic. It may happen that due to some reasons you may not find an invoice in S3 then do we follow the flow that we have today or error our or something else such as generate that invoice and store it in S3 for later access.
# Is the strategy to archive these PDF to some cheaper storage such as Amazon S3 Glacier in scope for this project or shall it be taken in later while working on archiving solution? - _For now, we should keep this out of scope of this project given it will lead to lot of open ended questions, dependent projects such as invoice lifecycle, archiving solution etc. and we have limited time to solve specific problems stated under reasons section above._

Hi [~accountid:6073f7ad9361560068adbda1] !

Thanks for raising this request.

*Acceptance rate blocking and retraining*

So this ticket has two sides to it. Acceptance rate blocking entails a considerable increased risk of reclassification _in itself._ Adding the ‘re-training’ would increase the feature’s inherent risk even more.

Our Product Legal team (global) assessed acceptance rate blocking some time ago (the assessment is [+here+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1T6o8EkgxMIuTWh1v6A4Abe8sVknV2sPtU7knhUFGZ9U/edit]). The whole assessment has this big disclaimer in red in the beginning of the doc: 

{quote}{color:#ff5630}*“General note for these screens: acceptance rate blocking is effectively non-defendable from the perspective of a reclassification risk. Should we decide to display these screens to our drivers, we are providing drivers with more evidence to claim that they are Bolt’s employees.* {color}{color:#ff5630}(…){color}{color:#ff5630}*”*{color}{quote}

*RH reclassification risk in Norway.* 

Norway is a medium-high risk market in terms of reclassification as it is. On top of that, as of 1 January 2024 Norwegian law changes the definition of an “employee” to "anyone who performs work for and is subordinate to another" and _employment status will be presumed_ - unless independence is _proved_ “overwhelmingly likely”_._ We are still at the assessment stage with this law update, but at least going forward, there’s for sure an increased risk that we will need to defend ourselves against employment-related claims and prove that drivers are not employed by us in Norway.

*In summary:* 

# *Acceptance rate blocking = high reclassification risk in itself.* 
# *Adding ‘re-training’ feature onto acceptance rate blocking = increased reclassification risk.*

We will leave it up to you to decide whether the commercial benefit outweighs the risk, i.e., whether you want to proceed with adding the new re-training and / or keeping acceptance rate blocking live in Norway, or not.

Please let me know your thoughts and if you have any questions.

I agree with [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] assessment on this and we are not in a position to spend legal resources on this topic as we don’t have the final approval to proceed with the launch yet. However, if we want to conduct market research we should limit questions on Uber specifically and focus on the ride-hailing industry as a whole. 

Having said that, information exchanges – that is the exchange of certain types of competitively sensitive information between competitors (such as price, cost, market, market share, customer, supplier or business or strategic plan information) can represent a significant risk for companies (as well as their management and boards). Generally speaking, the exchange of competitively sensitive information between competitors can dampen competitive rivalry by reducing competitors’ uncertainty about their rivals’ competitive and commercial responses.  More specifically, the exchange of competitively sensitive information between competitors can raise significant competition law risk under the Canadian [_Competition Act_|https://laws.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/C-34/page-11.html#h-89169]. However, in my general assessment this would only be a risk if the drivers are indeed employed by Uber (which is not the case as per my understanding) as they then can be seen as sharing such information +on behalf of Uber+. 

We have not done an in-depth analysis of the Canadian laws on this topic but recommend that you use the good practices advice from Julia below and focus on the market research as a whole rather than Uber specific research, at least in the way you phrase the questions. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

We fetch data from the write-ahead log of the database, so every committed change should be captured.

If you update the field and delete the row in the same transaction though, the update will never be visible outside of the transaction, and the database may therefore even decide to skip the update as optimization. So if you want to make sure that the update reaches the data lake, it’s better to do it in a separate transaction.

* Waiting time compensation: In some cases, couriers spend significant time waiting for the food to be ready in restaurants. This feature allows paying couriers for the time they spend waiting in restaurants.
* Courier adjustments: Adjustments made to the courier balance by local OPS team. incl. cash drop-off adjustments.
* Deposits: Bag deposits taken from couriers
* Adjusted Earnings: Total courier earnings after adjustments (Courier earnings + courier adjustments + waiting time compensations)
* Adjusted Earnings with courier tips: Total courier earnings after adjustments and courier tips (Courier earnings + courier adjustments + waiting time compensations + tips)
* Courier tips: Tips given to couriers by eaters
* Cash dropped off at providers: Applies to cash orders. Eaters can choose to pay by cash. In that case, courier pays the amount to the provider in cash (and later collects it from the eater)
* Cash picked up from clients: Applies to cash orders. This is the amount courier collects from the eater after paying cash to the provider for cash orders.
* Balance before period: Courier’s balance in the beginning of the week.
* Balance after period: Courier’s balance at the end of the week.

Without VAT values simply refer to the net amount for the above entries. With VAT entries are after VAT is added to Without VAT entries. A courier’s/fleet’s VAT liability is defined by “liable to VAT” flag in their profile (usually checked by the local team). And the VAT percentage is configured in city VAT settings (by local OPS team).

*_Note_*: the flag has been updated and is initially set to false in the current PR: {{enable_centralized_eta_v2}}



This aims to achieve the following behaviour:

* happy path: we receive an order with ETA stored in polling (i.e. “order_preparation_eta” is not null) → we show the ETA as expected
* “order_preparation_eta” is null for 1 polling session path: we show the spinning wheel for ETA for 5 seconds, until the next polling presents the ETA
* “order_preparation_eta” is null for more polling sessions path:we show the spinning wheel for ETA for 5 seconds, and afterwards we show the order without ETA

 

How to test?

# Activate the centralize flag: {{enable_centralized_eta_v2}}
# Create orders and notice that when an order is displayed, it will always have the ETA
# To make sure that such a case is replicated, watch the Charles logs and once we receive an “order_preparation_eta” = null, but the order was displayed alongside the ETA, then we have tested the behaviour
# Note that the <“order_preparation_eta” is null for more polling sessions path> is (should be :D ) highly unlikely to reproduce

Our approach is to request only for minimal viable information. We should seek documents that are legally and operationally mandatory and avoid asking for any additional information beyond that because this only adds extra friction.
This document is not a required one at the moment so it is not asked from the drivers anyways. 

Why do we not want optional documents? Three basic reasons:

* If only some drivers submit the document while others do not, it diminishes the document's value as it fails to provide a comprehensive and accurate picture of the data.
* If a document does not contribute critical information, questioning its necessity arises. Requesting non-critical documents leads to unnecessary data collection and utilisation of resources.
* Requesting unnecessary documents incurs processing costs, as local specialists must verify them, auto-acceptance team must determine their relevance, etc. This not only consumes time but also adds to the overall operational expenses without contributing substantially to the process.

However, before we deactivate it, we would like to know if there would be any implications to our business?

{code:sql}with cases as (
select 
	id as support_case_id
	, user_persona  
	, is_escalated_to_agent 
	, created as support_case_created
	, order_id 
	, city_id 
	, is_safety_related
from ng_customer_support.etl_tw_support_case 
where 1=1
	and user_persona in ('rider', 'driver')
	and date(created_date) >= date('2023-09-01')
	and date(created_date) < date('2023-12-01')
	and order_id is not null
	and is_incoming = true
),
calls as (
select 
	d.*
	, case when e.call_id is null then false else true end as order_has_call_s
	, e.caller_type
	, e.callee_type
	, case when e."result" = 'ANSWERED' then true
		when e."result" is not null and e."result" <> 'ANSWERED' then false
		else null end as at_least_one_call_was_answered
	, case when f.chat_id is null then false else true end as order_has_chat
	, row_number () over (partition by d.support_case_id order by e."result" asc) as filter_helper
from cases as d
left join comms.voip_metrics_calls as e
	on d.order_id = e.order_id
	and d.city_id = e.city_id
	and e.order_system = 'taxi'
	and date(e.emitted_at_hour) >= date('2023-06-01')
left join comms.chat_order as f
	on d.order_id = f.order_id
	and d.city_id = f.city_id
	and f.order_system = 'taxi'
	and date(f.created_date) >= date('2023-06-01')
),
calls_cases as (
select 
	*
from calls 
where filter_helper = 1
),
calls_cases_final as (
select 
	a.*
	, c.issue_title
	, c.is_internal as issue_is_internal
from calls_cases as a
left join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case_issue as b
	on a.support_case_id = b.support_case_id
left join ng_customer_support.support_issue_store_support_issue as c
	on b.issue_key = c.issue_key
)
select 
	user_persona
	, issue_title
	, issue_is_internal
	, is_escalated_to_agent
	, order_has_call_s
	, at_least_one_call_was_answered
	, order_has_chat
	, count(distinct support_case_id) as case_count
from calls_cases_final
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6,7{code}

Please disregard my above comment when I said that the transaction is B2C, this is not the case.

Most likely in Romania small-medium enterprises can be treated as a business for VAT purposes just with their registration number, as the first invoice corroborates (registration number is included). Both invoices are cross-border B2B and reverse-charge mechanism applies. 

The main point comes with the fact that, for a business (Provider in this case) to recover the input VAT they incurred in the above transactions, they need to have a valid VAT number. That means that since November, the provider is able to recover the VAT on the service that Bolt renders to it. But prior to November, they can not recover the VAT they incurred - it is a cost for them - because they did not have the VAT number yet, and this is why they are asking for the re-issuing of the invoices.

Please communicate to them that unfortunately, for legal reasons, we are not able to re-issue amended invoices with the current VAT number they hold, as the VAT number does not apply retrospectively and back then (period Aug-Oct) the Provider did not have a valid VAT number in place. Alternatively, the Provider may want to check with local tax advisors whether in Romania it is possible to recover input VAT retrospectively since they obtained the VAT number. 

(I disregard the latest, as it is purely a domestic VAT law question, but this is on their plate)

Timeline of a new legislation to be passed:

In principle the bill should be reviewed by the Parliament within 6 month after it is being registered.  In reality, it can take much longer or shorter depending on the urgency of the topic.
The process of passing new laws in the Ukrainian parliament is as follows:

# A bill is drafted with an explanatory note and a financial and legal assessment.  The bill is registered in the parliament and published on its website *- done in Oct*
# The bill is assigned to a parliamentary committee that is responsible for its preliminary examination. The committee (i.e. the tax committee in this case) prepares a report with its conclusions and recommendations, which may include amendments or alternative versions of the bill.  *- This is where we are*
# The bill is included in the agenda of a plenary session of the parliament and being considered by the parliament within six months from its registration. *i.e. by April 2024* (in principle)The bill is considered by the parliament in three readings. In the first reading, the parliament may approve the bill as a whole, reject it, or return it to the committee for further revision . In the second reading, the parliament discusses and votes on each article and amendment of the bill. The parliament may approve the bill as amended, reject it, *or postpone its consideration* . In the third reading, the parliament reviews and approves the final text of the bill.  *- Here can cause delays*
# If there is no delay and the bill has passed the vote, the approved bill is sent to the President for signature within ten days. The President may sign the bill into law, veto it partially or fully, or return it to the parliament with his proposals . If the President vetoes the bill, the parliament may override his veto by a two-thirds majority vote within 30 days .
# The law is officially promulgated by publishing it in the official newspaper of the parliament. The law comes into force on the day following its publication, unless otherwise specified in the law.  - I expect the effective date to be later than the publish date because it should give the gig workers time to do tax registration.

Hi [~accountid:5aa282eb1e5627213ac76f0e] Here are some of our initial findings, thoughts and considerations.

* Downstream impacts for Adaptive, they would need to complete a remodel (not sure of total impact)
* Upstream for Presto/FDW for journal creation (any templates they have built for Billing)
* Custom validations - would be possible and would probably simplify the maintenance after initial set up
* Account Posting Rules (APR) - updates required for new account codes, particularly in Spend and Revenue. Receivables and Payables etc, would be low impact as we would probably just renumber 1200 & 2100 to 12000 & 21000
* Ad hoc bank transactions templates
* Ad hoc payment templates 
* Allocations (need [~accountid:61f7dc37f5f5b80070c6540e] input here to understand the logic of the allocations, some definitions are based on ledger account code, e.g. All Workers Based Distribution. Would this continue or would we need to amend source conditions?)
* Local Chart of Account Mappings - We have 3 mappings in Prod, France, China & Poland. This is potentially a big piece of work to remap, both at Accounting side and for WD team.
* Reports - specifically some of the Financial Controlling composite reports have filters in them based on conditions of combinations of spend.
* Elimination Rules - NCI & Intercompany
* -Tax Declaration Definitions- - No impact
* External Journals - Payroll from Immedis (need to investigate further)
* External Journals - Interest Sweeps from Kyrbia (need to investigate further)



Moving from a 4 digit structure to a 5 digit structure would not be too much of an issue, we could update the existing account numbers and there would not be an impact on Account Posting Rules, for example, if we changed *1010: Bank Accounts - EUR* to +*10010*+*: Bank Accounts - EUR* then the Account Posting Rules would automatically update. This is easily changed and not a huge impact.

!image-20231205-092809.png|width=844,height=699!

If we want to move to a 1:1 Spend Cat:Ledger Account, we would need to create additional accounts, for example, 5110 into 51101 & 51102, recommendation here would be to dispose/disregard 5110 and create *51101 Cost of external repair* & *51102 Spare parts and accessories*

h3. Research findings

Two types of set-up:

* Order & Pay
** The order is initiated and paid by the eater, i.e. no interaction with the waiter or cashier. Relevant in cases where merchants want to optimise labour costs and enforce counter service.
** Upon arriving at a restaurant and being seated at a table, eaters will scan a QR code that will lead them to an UI where they can add items to a basket, checkout, and pay for the order. After the order was paid - it will be prepared by the provider and served. No additional items will be added to the order.
* Pay & Go
** The order is initiated by the waiter and paid by the eater, i.e. the waiter always comes to take the order. Relevant in cases when merchants prefer to keep table service, but see room to optimise the checkout process
** Upon arriving at a restaurant and being seated at a table, eaters will scan a QR code that will lead them to an UI where they can browse the menu and place an order with the waiter. At any point eaters can ask the waiter for more items which will be added to the initial order / basket created by the waiter. Eaters can pay at any moment, however any additional items ordered after the payment will result in a new order.

But, this is exactly why we are doing it 🙂 So we are not “sneaky” and cut off cents.

If we only use 2 decimals, the amount from the 3rd decimal will pile up but will never be paid to the partner. Or it will be a cost to us which we cannot explain - accounting-wise. By using the 3rd decimal and aggregating it:

a. if the decimal rounds up to a negative amount, we charge it as a debt (from their payout)

b. but, if it’s a positive amount, we also pay this .01 back to the provider - so they don’t lose this .01 in the long run.

I 8 § i diskrimineringslagen förbjuds diskriminering på grund av bland annat hälsotillstånd och funktionsnedsättning. Förutom direkt och indirekt diskriminering är även vägran att göra rimliga anpassningar sådan diskriminering som avses i diskrimineringslagen. Enligt 15 § i diskrimineringslagen ska de som tillhandahåller varor och tjänster göra sådana ändamålsenliga och rimliga anpassningar som behövs i det enskilda fallet för att göra det möjligt för personer med funktionsnedsättning att på lika villkor som andra få varor och tjänster som tillhandahålls allmänheten. Enligt 23 § i diskrimineringslagen har den som blivit utsatt för diskriminering eller repressalier rätt att få gottgörelse av den myndighet, arbetsgivare, utbildningsanordnare eller tillhandahållare av varor eller tjänster som i strid med denna lag har diskriminerat eller utsatt honom eller henne för repressalier. I de fall som anmälts till ombudsmannen har tjänsteleverantörerna också konstaterats vara gottgörelseskyldiga beträffande den diskriminering som inträffat.

Många som rör sig med assistenthund upplever att i synnerhet restauranger är svåra objekt när man har med sig en hund. Tjänsteleverantören hänvisar ofta till att det inte är tillåtet att ha med sig djur till livsmedelslokaler. Enligt 18 § i jord- och skogsbruksministeriets förordning om livsmedelshygienen i anmälda livsmedelslokaler (16.5.2017/291) får en hund som assisterar en person med funktionsnedsättning följa med till en livsmedelslokals kundutrymmen. Många diskrimineringsfall av denna typ kan undvikas genom att öka medvetenheten om lagstiftningen som gäller assistenthundar. Det är också viktigt att personer med funktionsnedsättning är medvetna om sin rätt att vara verksamma och röra sig tillsammans med hund, eftersom diskrimineringen annars lätt hamnar i skymundan och fortsätter.

* en vakt i en butik följer efter en person som tillhör en etnisk minoritet

h2. Man får inte välja sina kunder på diskriminerande grunder

Ibland kan diskriminering orsakas av missuppfattningen om att en varu- eller tjänsteleverantör helt fritt skulle få välja sina kunder. {color:#ff5630}*Butiker och restauranger får välja sina kunder, men det får inte ske på diskriminerande grunder* {color}såsom till exempel ursprung, funktionsnedsättning eller sexuell läggning.

In-App messages are an interesting privacy topic.

I am very busy with more important inquiries atm, but I will get back to you sometime this week to provide further explanation.

In short, there is case law in the EU, which will label in-App notification direct marketing (with all subsequent limitations) in case it actually resembles a personalised communication (an email), and is personalised.

For general notifications that are not intended for promotion, there is no hard rule that the user must have an option not to receive them.

For now, the policy of Bolt is that in-App communications are not to be considered direct marketing. This can change next year as the privacy team will assess this problem further to understand the risks.

I am grateful for the examples of the comms.

Hi again [~accountid:615c1af4048360006a44e16c] ,

To further add to Michelle’s advice yesterday, the key here is that if anyone is guilty of having discriminated this rider by refusing them to take their service animal on the ride, it would be the driver, not Bolt. Please see some further details below. 

*Under Finnish law, everyone must be treated equally in* *_private services offered to the public_**.* This includes transportation services, such as taxi rides (provided by the driver) and electronic services (also referred to as e-services), such as the Bolt platform (provided by Bolt).

*The driver is the one providing transportation services*. Refusing to provide transportation services to people because they have a service animal is comparable to refusing because of a disability (diabetes it seems in this context - and service animals are like medical aid), which is discrimination and illegal. The same likely applies to prompting that the rider orders pet-ride instead, because it would ultimately mean that it’s more expensive for a person with a disability to ride than for a non-disabled person.

*Bolt only provides the electronic services relating to the Bolt platform.* Bolt does not provide any transportation services. Discrimination by Bolt in connection with providing the e-services could, for example, be if we wrote on the website that people with service animals are not allowed to use our app/order rides. 

I agree with [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7]'s advice, i.e:

{quote}“We should 

1) inform the rider that the driver is the person providing transportation services and that Bolt provides a platform services and 

2) state that Bolt does of course not accept any type of discrimination and does not want to support this. (Any wordings should go through PR first). “{quote}

Please let me know the status on the following: 

* Have you replied anything to the rider in line with the above, and did you have a chance to talk to PR?  
* Has the rider requested a specific compensation, and has compensation been discussed with Local Ops?

Please let me know if you have any questions on the above, or need any further assistance from a legal point of view.

Many thanks.

Hi,

Thanks for raising a very interesting and surprisingly hard question. 

Easy part first. As Jingle Bells copyright has expired, its melody can be freely used. 

However, it is unclear whether or not we can freely (commercially) use the sound created through Online Sequencer. Online Sequencer has no terms of use, at least I did not find any. In their forum, users have asked about it and they replied ([LINK|https://onlinesequencer.net/forum/archive/index.php?thread-4056.html]): 

----

“Online Sequencer doesn't claim any ownership of your work. Licensing for the instrument sounds used is kind of a gray area though since *we didn't record/synthesize them from scratch, we put them together from other soundfonts and effect plugins that are available for free online.* [Here's a very long debate|https://musescore.org/en/node/305408] on another website about this issue. But it seems like the consensus is that you wouldn't get in trouble.

If you really want to be sure everything is licensed properly, you could export a MIDI file and use another program ([TiMidity++ is an example|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TiMidity%2B%2B]) to render it to .mp3 using any General MIDI soundfont that has a license allowing commercial use.”

----

The fact that something is available free online does not automatically mean that its commercial use is allowed. Therefore, I am not able to confirm 100% that music created via Online Sequencer can be commercially used. Probably the risk is very low, because I can’t imagine how a potential rights holder can understand and prove the infringement.  

Based on the above, our options are a) to accept the risk (in an unlikely worst case scenario we just need to pay to the rights holder), or b) choose alternatives:

# Use a music sequencer that clearly allows commercial use;
# Play music on an instrument and record it ourselves 🙂

Best,

Indrek

Looks like there’s a bug in manifest merger when the same permission is declared via {{uses-permission-sdk-23}} and {{uses-permission-sdk}} tags at the same time. There is a [suggested solution|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/44298951/android-manifest-duplicate-permissions] that uses {{tools:node="removeAll"}} attribute, but it removes all {{uses-permission-sdk-23}} tags from all manifests in the app which is dangerous and can lead to broken functionality and hard-to-debug issues.

Since having both {{uses-permission-sdk-23}} and {{uses-permission-sdk}} tags in the app manifest has shown to be safe in production, I suggest to keep things as is and don’t remove {{uses-permission-sdk-23}} tags.

Hi [~accountid:5d8df399c7d4e30dc2836580] 

*Quick answer:* provided Driver Score is deployed in the same way as the UK (no blocking/penalising on scorings for drivers) this should be fine and is considered low risk at present. 

*Context for answer*

Anusha has done some digging with the Product Legal Team to confirm that BQS (Behavioural Quality System) is the old version of Driver Score. Here is the fact pattern as we understand it presently between the UK and Ireland (mapping it out for future reference if you need it):

*UK - Driver Score*

* The former BQS system was problematic in the UK for employment reasons (as you are well versed in so I wont explain this further) and the proposed newer Driver Score system was going to have the same issues, so deployment was going to be restricted at best if this went ahead to simply be a monitoring tool without repercussions to drivers.
* As you’ve rightly recalled, the business did make a decision during Project Blue to remove Driver Score entirely given it had no use case in the UK (based on Josh’s analysis at the time and the fact we didn’t actually use it as it was commercially intended - for control) so it was going to be removed from all UK TnCs with the launch of PB. This was because litigious Drivers were referencing this as a control measure against Bolt (similar to Uber v Aslam) and we wanted to avoid providing any further ammunition in proceedings. This has been raised in our defence in the class action as a point of contention. 
* Because PB launch was halted, Driver Score hasn’t yet been removed from our TnCs (this can happen in our next TnC upgrade with Bolt Flex in Q1, which we should discuss soon) and therefore Driver Score in the UK is just the name we give as an umbrella term to describe *Activity Score* and *Configuration Rate* which have remained in place.
* Christopher in your team confirmed for me that it still remains the case that ‘Driver Score’ does not penalise the drivers or exert any control irrespective of whether we call it Driver Score, Activity Score or Configuration Rate. We have justified keeping Activity Score and Configuration rate for commercial purposes and that some drivers actually like to see this - however - we may want to re-visit our language on this in future to avoid misunderstandings. 

*Ireland - Driver Score*

* In Ireland, reclassification risks are lower given its a taxi market and drivers can ply for hire (similar to black cabs). 
* However, that doesn’t mean it’s completely risk free and some UK cases have involved taxi drivers in employment matters so it would be naive to assume they will never eventuate in Ireland. 
* To date we have not seen anything alarming come up as scoring relating risks for Ireland and Aisling is well tuned to this kind of thing, which is why we can still stand behind considering this Driver Score as being low risk and fine to proceed if it’s similar to the UK. 
* *Next steps:* We will continue to monitor any local employment proceedings for reclass risks and flag as needed. We would recommend a decision is made on Driver Score language and this is also included for the Ireland TnC upgrade that we’ve pencilled in for Q1 given the local TnCs are well overdue.

Many thanks, 

Clarissa

Hi, [~accountid:712020:adc75bb7-f145-4fbb-b5a0-0536b95ff918]! I can provide you with some insights too.

The idea is to create a database of our employees within the Salv’s system and compare the names of our suppliers and potential customers with the names of employees to see whether there are any connections between them. To do this we will need to upload the list of our employees to the Salv’s system before checks will take place.

The database of names of our employees will be stored in the Salv’s system. They are using AWS server located in Frankfurt. You can check out this [ticket |https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-23334]and the agreement signed with Salv that contains data processing agreement attached to this reply (Annex 1 to the Service Agreement).

In theory, this database can be accessed by certain employees of Salv (CS and Data science team members can see everything that is in the system) and employees of Bolt that were granted the access to the Salv’s system. However, the access to this database can be limited by defining user roles. The information about different user roles is [here|https://salv.notion.site/Users-0a4de9c605764978904a4a1c2749c071]. In short, from Bolt’s side there will be limited amount of users with Admin or extended rights, who will be able to see all the information and the database of employees, but there can be users with roles that have limited access that won’t be able to see the database, namely:

* People running ad-hoc checks - just work on alerts or do manual search. The correct user role would be: AML Agent Limited. They will be able to see an entry from the database only if there is a match between the suppliers/clients and the employee database, they won’t be able to see the entire database.
* IT - someone who will be responsible for IT issues like API connection and webhooks. This person cannot see any information about alerts or the database. The correct user role would be: IT Admin

Hello Sabina! 

The agent presses the call button, speaks to the caller, then hangs up the phone and immediately the agents are presented with the wrap-up window where they can quickly enter both a public reply and an internal note of the situation in a matter of minutes, and then close the enquiry without leaving the window. When they close that window, the query just automatically becomes solved and they can immediately start another query. 

Of course, agents can close the window and then create a response, which would reduce the time, but agents who have developed the habit of doing the description in this wrap-up window (when they can select a tag) in all call requests, would comply forget it for the cases where no issue tag should be added. 

In this case, when the query cannot be closed without a tag, the agents forget that they cannot do it through the wrap-up window, so they spend 2-3 minutes writing to the interlocutor that they were unable to contact them, ask them to let them know if they still need help, they leave a message in that window, try to close it and immediately see the error that they cannot. This means they need to close that window and spend another couple of minutes again creating a new message in the main BH window. The whole process then takes 4-5 minutes instead of 2 minutes because of the encountered error. 

For example, in this [situation|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/298390742], the agent encountered the above error because she is used to closing the query in that wrap-up window and got lost and had to close the query with an incorrect tag. 

I hope that by expanding on the situation I have helped to clarify how the wrap-up window works. But if you need more of my help, feel free to write. 😊

Please find below answers to your questions:

* Why the law obliges us to collect these docs? What is the purpose?

With the new law the Ministry is trying to regulate platform work. They want to have better control over fleets and their employees (drivers/couriers) and oblige fleets to employ drivers (and pay all relevant benefits and taxes) and not engage them only as contractors. 

* Which docs should we collect, can you please specify all of them?

The law does not explicitly prescribe which documents platforms should collect but it prescribes an obligation on platforms to inform the Ministry about the relationship between the fleet and the driver/courier i.e. if it is employment or only contractual. 

* When we collected them, what will we do with them?

I guess we will save them for the duration of the contractual relationship with the fleet. The only purpose of collecting this info is to be able to inform the Ministry. 

Fleets will be obliged to provide us with this info on a monthly basis and we will need to share the info with the Ministry also on a monthly basis. 

* How long will we retain them? Do we know the retention period?

I guess we will save them for the duration of the contractual relationship with the fleet only for the purpose of being able to prove that we have collected these info from drivers/couriers in case of nay dispute with the Ministry. 

* Which team will collect these docs, when (sign-up process), and how (from fleets, directly by couriers to Bolt)?

The local Ops team will collect them directly from Fleets. 

* Where will we store these docs?

Probably Google Docs

* Which team is responsible for deleting these docs from our systems?

Bolt local Ops

If the user has a negative Bolt Balance and travels to a country with a different currency, they won't be able to view their balance on the app anymore. Therefore, they won't be able to add funds to it or clear the debt. To resolve this issue, follow the steps outlined below:

*Step 1: Confirm charge details*

* Open User Balance > [Transaction history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] in Admin Panel
* Confirm there’s been a charge that caused a negative balance
* Look for a Booking that has: 💳 failed 🟢success
* Open the ride that caused the charge and check the date

*Step 2: Verify the cause*

* Open the Fraud > Calculations > [User page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults]
* Look for a decision REJECT TOP UP
** To ensure that the user cannot use the app because of debt, check for rows created on the same day or within one day.
* Is there a REJECT TOP UP decision?
** If yes, refund the trip that caused the debt to the user’s Bolt Balance
** If not, don’t refund the trip; advise the user they can use the app.


If you need any further information, let me know.

Hello Kacper Kulaga 

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

Unless it is our mistake, e.g. the value, subject of the sale, or NIP number is wrongly stated by us, then we reissue the invoice. And we need to report VAT for the new invoice.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

We have two options here to implement this request. [~accountid:5dfb984e9a14250cb69f1697] is going to focus tomorrow on implementing the 2nd option. If he succeeds, we will handover to SRE team otherwise Kostia will further work on it. {{ETA}}: Next week mid.

Sure we have a clause in the Rides T&C’s (copied below for convenience) but it mitigates the risk of the user A submitting any claims due to his data becoming available to user B. It’s for the case the user A is suffering the damage.

With the case at hand however the issue is that it’s the user A who is in breach towards user B (and his employer). Surely user A is to blame here eventually, but question for Bolt in my view is can we accept such a gap in design, should/can we mitigate it and how. 

The fact that we don’t/are not able to ensure that no such connection is made between user A’s and B’s Rides account is highly problematic. For me also the scale of the matter is unclear, e.g. can user B’s private card be exposed as well (or why only the Business payment method became available to user A) and is user B’s personal data exposed to user A as well.

Also updated config to forward the package to GitHub packages of Bolt directly to GitHub via nexus not to nexus. 

The main reason, it’s that nexus and jfrog work differently with GitHub. 

Format of package mirrored from github in Nexus: [http://nexus_domain/repo_name/-/package_name/hash|http://nexus_domain/repo_name/-/hash]

For jfrog is: 

[http://jfrog_domain/artifactory/api/npm/repo_name/package_version/package_name/hash|http://jfrog_domain/artifactory/api/npm/repo_name/package_version/package_name/hash]

That is why migration from nexus to jfrog quite painful.. Because if information about package path taken from yarn.lock, jfrog not able to find such packages nowhere, because it doesn’t understand format of it.

* _General Terms -_ *Agency fee* means the fee payable by the Partner to Bolt per every event of sale of the Partner’s Goods through the Bolt Food Platform for the provision of agency services to the Partner.
** *Note!* Incredibly difficult to read in English. The Romanian version is easier to understand.
* [@viktoriadebora.raudberg|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U05FSLV7PHP]’s input:  Bolt and the Partner will agree on the percentage (aka *Agreed Percentage*) that will serve as the basis for calculating the Agency Fee. However, the Agency Fee is the actual fee that the Partner needs to pay Bolt calculated by applying the Agreed Percentage to the gross Good Price. So, if we imagine that the Agreed Percentage is 20% and the gross Goods Price is 10 EUR, then Agency Fee will be 2 EUR. The Partner owes Bolt the fee, not a percentage per se.
** We need to define then the Agreed Percentage in the Special Terms to make it easier to follow.
** Let’s make it clear what “Fee” means everywhere.
** As a general rule, the Partners first follow the Special Terms and then relate to the General T&Cs.

*Marketplace Fees*:

* General Terms - *Marketplace Fees -* means all such (the arrangements and functionalities of the Bolt Food Platform that facilitate the use of on-demand delivery services provided by the Couriers ) *service fees* and costs that Bolt may implement under Section 6.2 for covering the cost of the Marketplace and the availability of the Couriers.
** Note! How does one “implement a cost”?
* General Terms - 6.2 Fees - Bolt has the right to implement *Marketplace Fees* in accordance with the principles of dynamic pricing by (i) applying service fees in order to cover the cost of making courier services available at the Marketplace, or (ii) forwarding the cost of making delivery services available at the Marketplace provided however that the sum of *Agency Fee* and *Marketplace Fees* will not exceed the *Agreed Percentage*.
** *Note!* Are principles of dynamic pricing defined or we use it as a generic term?
** *Note!* It’s not clear that the Marketplace Fees could be Payable by the Partner, i.e. deducted from the Agreed Percentage.
** *Note*! costs are not “forwarded”.
** *Note*! I do understand our limitations given courier reclassif risks, but we can structure it a lot better.

*Agreed Percentage*:

* General Terms - *Agreed Percentage -* is the percentage agreed in the Special Terms that serves as the basis for the calculation of the Agency Fee.
** *Note!* We need to define then the Agreed Percentage in the Special Terms to make it easier to follow and make the reasoning of [@viktoriadebora.raudberg|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U05FSLV7PHP] easy to understand.
* General Terms - 6.1 Fees - In consideration for Bolt’s services as the agent for mediation of the Sales Agreements the Partner shall pay the *Agency Fee* to Bolt per every Order of the Client made through the Bolt Food Platform. The *Agency Fee* is calculated as the *Agreed Percentage* from the aggregate net Price earned by the Partner from the Orders placed through the Bolt Food Platform during a particular reference period.
** *Note!* aggregated net Price - > this is not correct and subject to interpretation. It is the Gross Value (incl VAT ).
** *Note!* Take notes above into consideration.

*Service Fees*:

* General Terms - *Service Fees* - means the fees payable by the Partner according to Section 6.3.
** *Note*! These are first introduced in Section 6.2
* General Terms - 6.3 - The Partner shall also pay *Service Fees* to Bolt for the use of the tablet (if applicable) and software, in accordance with the Special Terms. In addition Bolt may charge the Partner a fee for running a marketing campaign which shall be agreed between the Parties.
** *Note*! Can we write that Service Fees can consist of a), b), c)

*Additional Fees*:

* General Terms - 4.9 - The Partner may not charge the Client any additional fees for the packaging of the Goods, unless agreed otherwise in the Partner Specific conditions.
** *Note*! Partner Specific conditions are Special Terms? If so, let’s be consistent with the wording.

*Applicable Fees*:

* General Terms - 7.4 - Within three business days from the expiry of each reference period Bolt will issue an invoice to the Partner for the *Agency Fee,* *Service Fees* and any *other applicable fees* for a given reference period. If any payments are to be made by Bolt to the Partner in relation to the reference period, the Partner will issue an invoice to Bolt.
** *Note*! We defined so many fees that <Applicable Fees> seam other fees on top. Partners will ask for explanations. Are these also included in the *Agreed Percentage*?

(2) For the commission of the same acts, if they have been committed by a public official, using its official position, or a group of persons according to a prior agreement, or for illegal movement of several person across the State border in one time,

the applicable punishment is the deprivation of liberty for a period of up to five years or temporary deprivation of liberty, or probationary supervision, or community service, or fine, with or without confiscation of property.

(3) For the commission of the same acts, if they have been committed by an organised group or they have resulted in serious consequences, or also who commits illegal movement of a large number of persons, that is, more than five persons at one time, across the State border,

EST:

Päring Euroopa Uurimismääruse (EIO) raames kriminaalasjas Pnm 99/22/2205

Antud Euroopa uurimis määr us on saabunud
kriminaalmenetlus seadustikus sätestatud normidele (vt KrMS § 489-37 jj) ja arvestades asjaolusid, et Bolt emafirma on Eestis. Tulenevalt KrMS § 215 lg 1 kohaselt on uurimisasutuste ja prokuratuuri määruste ja nõuete täitmine kohustuslik. Samuti võib KrMS § 214 lg 1 alusel kohtueelse menetluse andmeid avaldada üksnes prokuratuuri loal ning määratud ulatuses. Tegemist on välisriigi kriminaalmenetlusega ning teistest riikidest saadud teabe kaitseks ei ole võimalik meil välisriigi menetluse kohta andmeid avaldada.

Samuti täpsustame, et KrMS § 15-2 tulenevalt kehtivad ka kriminaalmenetluses isikuand me te töötlemise reeglid, sh on menetlejal õigus töödelda isikuandmeid, sealhulgas eriliiki isikuandmeid, mis onvajalikud kohtueelse menetluse jakohtumenetluse läbiviimiseks, tõendite kogumiseks, kriminaalasjas tehtud lahendi täitmisele pööramiseks, jälitustoimingu tegemiseks või muu käesolevas seaduses sätestatud eesmärgi saavutamiseks. Sellest tulenevalt ei ole teil õigust GDPRi põhjusel meie nõudekirjast keelduda.

Täiendavalt selgitame, et keeldumise korral võib KrMS § 215 lg 3 tulenevalt kohustuse täitmata jätnud menetlusosalist, kriminaalmenetluses osalevat muud isikut või menetlusvälist isikut eeluurimiskohtunik prokuratuuri taotlusel trahvida kohtumääruse alusel. Lisaks on võimalik taotleda ka Bolti kontori läbiotsimist taotletud andmete saamiseks.

Vastuse krüpteerimisel palume valida asutuseks „Politsei- ja Piirivalveamet (PPA) 70008747“ ning vastus edastada e-posti aadressile: [ppa@politsei.ee|mailto:ppa@politsei.ee].

The information requested is necessary to continue the investigation and discover the truth, and does not conflict with the protection of personal data.

The Criminal Procedure Code does not have a rule regarding the duty of collaboration of other entities with the judicial authorities (Public Prosecutor's Office or Judge), we have to help ourselves, in accordance with the provisions of article 4 of the CPP, of the Procedure Code Civil, namely article 417.

The article referred to in paragraph 1 determines, as a general principle in this matter, that: “all people, whether or not they are parties to the case, have the duty to provide their collaboration in discovering the truth, responding to what they is asked, submitting to the necessary inspections, providing whatever is requested and carrying out the acts that are determined”.

In the same sense, art. providing documents and providing the requested information and clarifications in a duly justified manner according to the competence to be exercised, within the limits of the law, and without prejudice to the applicable secrecy regimes”.

In other words, the law enshrines an authentic duty of collaboration that falls not only on the parties, but also on third parties outside the process.
In turn, art. process (…) the judge may sentence the defendant to pay a fee fixed between 1 UC and 3 UC”.

The basis for providing the requested information therefore results from the provisions of article 417, no. 2, 1st part of the Code of Civil Procedure, and failure to respond may be sanctioned with a fine under the provisions of in articles 521, no. 2 of the Criminal Procedure Code and 27, no. 1 and 4 of the Procedural Costs Regulation.

In view of the above, I request that, within 10 days, a response be given to the request in the attached Email, under penalty of being sentenced to a fine, in accordance with the aforementioned legal provisions."

The message created is set in a helper [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/develop/src/async/mq/publish/MqPublisherHelper.ts#L49|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/develop/src/async/mq/publish/MqPublisherHelper.ts#L49]

before the message is stored in the DB.

Basically we have messages sitting too long in DB before the publishing cron picks then up and publishes.

Theory: the updates come in bursts and they sit in the db for few secs until the MqDBPublisher manages to work through them.

Possible options:

* remove the MqPublisher - publish messages directly - that would resolve the problem with the message age, but we would loose the transactioanlity guaranteed by the implementation
* tune the config params to see if we can get better throughput: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/89c3fe6c44417054401de45417ab2fbc4daef16a/common/payment/paymentStatusUpdatePublisher.ts#L31|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/89c3fe6c44417054401de45417ab2fbc4daef16a/common/payment/paymentStatusUpdatePublisher.ts#L31]

Hello, let me add my comment from privacy side.

Some time ago, we had a similar request regarding the insurance process in Portugal: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-23796|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-23796|smart-link] , where we provided our insights.

After performing our analysis, it seems that sharing the name+phone number of drivers and fleets with the insurance company representing a rider is in line with the GDPR, we can proceed with the practice as-is.

We assessed the option of relying on driver's consent -> this would not be feasible in practice, as we would overcomplicate the process, especially if the consent is not received. Consent is also likely not the appropriate legal basis under the GDPR in this case.

Speaking in legal terms, we do not need to obtain consent for the data sharing to be legitimate. In such cases, we can use another legal basis - our legitimate interest. In other words, the GDPR does not block us from sharing personal data if we have a legal basis to do so.

When it comes to fleets, you are correct, they are not [usually] covered by the GDPR, so:

* We would be sharing driver data upon our legitimate interest (as this data is protected under the GDPR).
* We can share fleet data, as it is not protected under the GDPR.

Let me know if further explanations would be needed.

[FinReg Playbook|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AZ6R3pQcPhwHNTbSdXytaZeG3T1CvIgO0N50WP1DcK4/edit#heading=h.imryovoigxjf], section “Fees” → [FinReg Guidelines on Fees|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cT0_tjXE4e4dniJGBU_T6-A2KHLkasM_0IBdl0EQszg/edit#heading=h.f21j2r5mzr]:

* In EU, Bolt’s rights to charge fees from the passenger are restricted. 
* We should +avoid+ fees, which could indicate we also offer services to passengers in relation to conclusion/negotiation of transportation agreement. Such fees, among others, could be for us helping the customer to find driver; etc.
* We +could+ apply fees which do not relate to us negotiating the conditions of the transportation agreement for the benefit of the passenger.

For detailed FinReg approval, please use the “[Template for validating new fees|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cT0_tjXE4e4dniJGBU_T6-A2KHLkasM_0IBdl0EQszg/edit#heading=h.v1gm7hamhwn4]” (as annexed to the guidelines). My suggestion is for Product/Legal to approach this matter as pan-EU (if not globally), to agree upon a common scalable solution and avoid the need to sign fee setups off country by country. At minimum, we can later go back to the PT sign-off documentation and use it for future sign-offs too.

In the current case, I am confused about the setup. You say that Bolt Ops charges the fee, but the fee is invoiced from the passenger by the fleet. To my understanding, this is not legally possible: If it is Bolt Ops charging the fee, then it should also be invoiced by Bolt Ops. If it is invoiced by the fleet, it would be legal income of the fleet, which I assume we do not want it to be. Also, ANA is invoicing us, not the fleet.

Hello Alan Dahi,

Thank you for your inquiry, which was received by us on December 2, 2023.

In relation to your request on the *retention period for data subject rights requests at Bolt,* we must point out that currently, we do not have a specific retention period in place for support cases related to data subject
rights requests. These cases are stored within the user’s active account and thereafter for the duration
they are needed for reference and resolution. 

To further enhance our data management procedures, we are actively working on implementing a
retention and deletion policy specifically for these support cases. This policy will define the appropriate
period for retaining such cases to balance user needs and data security.

To address your question related to *phone number change in the app*, we have to advise you that you can change your phone number directly in the app. To edit your phone number, follow these steps:

* Tap on the menu icon (3 horizontal lines)
* Tap on _View profile_
* Select _Edit profile_
* Locate the piece of information you want to change
* Select _Edit_
* Update the details
* Your information will be updated automatically, but you may be required to verify your details.

If you update *your phone number*, you will receive a verification request to your new phone number via SMS. Make sure you verify your new phone number following the instructions in SMS sent by Bolt. Once the phone number is verified, it will be changed in your profile automatically.

When you update your personal information in the Bolt app, the changes are also applied to the Bolt Food app.


Sincerely,
Bolt

Hi [~accountid:63314e9e9b32cfef93265252] I have read the Proposal Act and these are my brief conclusions:

*Clause 2 (3)*

l_obistje domaća ili strana fizička ili pravna osoba koja lobira i kojaje upisana u Registar lobista te podrazumijeva:_ 

_a) lobiste koji lobiraju za korisnike lobiranja, uključujući konzultante koji se bave lobiranjem i profesionalne lobiste_ 

*_b) lobiste koji lobiraju u ime poslodavca kod kojeg su zaposleni, ili_* 

_c) lobiste koji predstavljaju profesionalne, poslovne ili druge sektorske interese, uključujući profesionalna, gospodarska i interesna udruženja, nevladine udruge i organizacije civilnog društva._

* This means that in case you or anyone else will be lobbying on Bolt’s behalf this person  would be considered a lobbyist and would need to register as one.

*Clause 2 (3)*

_korisnici lobiranja su pravne ili fizičke osobe i drugi zakonom uređeni_ *_oblici udruživanja_* _fizičkih ili pravnih osoba, uključujući i njihove podružnice, u ime kojih lobist obavlja lobiranje_

* It is not really clear what is meant by *zakonom uredeni oblici udruzivanja,* depending on this there is possibility that anyone representing Bolt would be excluded from this Act. 



*Clause 4 (c)*

_Lobiranjem se ne smatra aktivnost osoba kada sudjeluju kao stručnjaci na sastancima, sjednicama ili konzultacijama o pitanjima koja se odnose na pripremu nacrta zakona, drugih propisa, općih akata te strateških i planskih dokumenata na poziv ili na inicijativu tijela zakonodavne ili izvršne vlasti, tijela državne uprave, odnosno tijela jedinica lokalne ili područne (regionalne) samouprave, bilo da djeluju za naknadu ili besplatno_

* my understanding is that our commenting of the laws and participating in the meetings with the ministry  connected with the implementation of new laws would not be considered as lobbying



*If what you do falls under this law (depending on the interpretation of Clause 2(3)) Then you would need to register as a lobbyist - and file an annual report about any lobbying activities.* 



_Pri najavi lobiranja, lobist je dužan predstaviti se lobiranoj osobi, dokazati daje upisan u Registar lobista, navesti svrhu i cilj te korisnika lobiranja za kojeg lobira._

_Podaci iz Registra lobista su javno dostupni._

_Lobist je dužan podnijeti izvještaj o provedenim lobiranjima u elektroničkim putem na propisanom obrascu.jednom godišnje do 31. siječnja tekuće godine za prethodnu godinu_

[~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] please see my comment of QFC reyirements(4. october). 
- *Processing of sensitive data* (also biometric data and criminal data) requires a proper legal basis ([Art 12 of the Act)|https://qfcra-en.thomsonreuters.com/rulebook/article-12-processing-sensitive-personal-data]. One of them is “explicit written consent”. If we are not comfortable with our consent regime, there is also the possibility to ask for a [permission |https://qfcra-en.thomsonreuters.com/rulebook/application-permit]but i do not know how long it will take the authority to decide

- *Privacy Notice:* besides a description of the applicable safeguards (letter F of point 3 of the rules) the requirements are similar to the GDPR.

- *Int. Transfer (EU):* For processing of Personal Data that involves the transfer of the Personal Data to a Recipient located in a jurisdiction outside the QFC  the Data Protection Office has decided  that EU Member states have an adequate level of protection, so transfers do not require any specific authorisation or notification to the Data Protection Office. The US is not on the list ([https://www.qfc.qa/-/media/project/qfc/qfcwebsite/documentfiles/resource-center/data-protection/data-transfers/qfc-data-protection-office-list-of-adequate-jurisdictions.pdf|https://www.qfc.qa/-/media/project/qfc/qfcwebsite/documentfiles/resource-center/data-protection/data-transfers/qfc-data-protection-office-list-of-adequate-jurisdictions.pdf])

- *Controller obligations:* 
--> RoPA
--> DPAs with processors
--> Data breach notification
--> DPIA
--> No DPO necessary, No registration as a controller necessary

So in a case like this, the rider tried to change the destination but we did not let him due to suspicious irregular activity (this can often apply to new users for example, or the stop being too far, or related users with suspicious history etc). We actively send a notification about this. So they knew that we would not allow them to do this and tried to circumvent our decision by asking the driver to do this anyway.

In these situations, the drivers should simply not accept the request. They should understand that this can lead to a forced failed payment and any ride that is not properly logged is basically a ghost ride. 

So we can refund the users and NOT compensate the drivers. I believe ultimately this would make it so drivers don’t accept this in the future, whereas it’s much harder to control user behaviour even through refunds.

I hope that this is clear but don’t hesitate to respond here if you have any other questions.

Best,

If the user has a negative Bolt Balance and travels to a country with a different currency, they won't be able to view their balance on the app anymore. Therefore, they won't be able to add funds to it or clear the debt. To resolve this issue, follow the steps outlined below:

*Step 1: Confirm charge details*

* Open User Balance > [+Transaction history+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] in Admin Panel
* Confirm there’s been a charge that caused a negative balance
* Look for a Booking that has: 💳 failed 🟢success
* Open the ride that caused the charge and check the date

*Step 2: Verify the cause*

* Open the Fraud > Calculations > [+User page+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults]
* Look for a decision REJECT TOP UP
** To ensure that the user cannot use the app because of debt, check for rows created on the same day or within one day.
* Is there a REJECT TOP UP decision?
** If yes, refund the trip that caused the debt to the user’s Bolt Balance
** If not, don’t refund the trip; advise the user they can use the app.

If you need any further information, let me know. Best Regards,

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *4/12/2023.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

* The purposes for which we process personal data;

* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Bolt
